{{Short description|Quartic surface in projective 3-space}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Weddle surface''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Thomas Weddle|last=Weddle|first=Thomas|year=1850|loc=footnote on page 69}}, is a [[quartic surface]] in 3-dimensional [[projective space]], given by the locus of vertices of the  family of cones passing through 6 points in [[general position]].

Weddle surfaces have 6 nodes and are [[birational]] to [[Kummer surface]]s.
